requirements.expected: Interactive section headings always set an explicit readable foreground color on the dark Prompt Kit surface.

Search ranks IDs, names, keywords, synonyms, types, and use-case metadata ahead of incidental prompt-body text for matching and recommendation relevance; visible library results are subsequently rendered in chronological numeric prompt order.
Existing SYNONYMS mappings remain active and partial query terms may resolve related synonym keys such as close -> closeout.
When strong metadata or synonym matches exist, copyContent-only matches do not flood the visible result set.
Users can favorite and unfavorite prompt cards; favorite IDs persist in browser localStorage without repository or server writes.

Legacy requirement ID retained for compatibility: Favorites are exposed as an explicit local filter rather than silently promoted ahead of earlier prompt numbers. The default library and Favorites-filtered result set remain chronological, and saved prompt identities are not duplicated or renumbered.
Favorite controls expose an accessible label and aria-pressed state and do not trigger card copy/open actions.

A separate visible Tutorial / Find My Prompt control preserves the existing Add Prompt action, uses three compact context questions plus one adaptive live-registry choice by default, asks no more than five bounded questions, and returns one primary recommendation with no more than two related options.

The fourth question is generated from current registry/search evidence rather than a fixed prompt-ID map; an optional fifth specialist question appears only when the user asks to browse beyond the adaptive candidates.

Every current Prompt Kit registry record is directly reachable through the optional specialist question, which renders the live PROMPTS collection and may filter it through the shared search engine without a hard-coded prompt-ID routing table.

Questionnaire answers are translated into normal search phrases and routed through filterPromptsForQuery against current PROMPTS; per-question evidence is de-duplicated before accumulation, and the specialist fallback also uses the current registry rather than a hard-coded prompt-ID recommendation table.
Questionnaire results resolve current PROMPTS registry records and expose their existing names and copy content rather than duplicating or fabricating prompt bodies.

The recommendation result and every opened prompt expose a structured current-to-next workflow using each live registry record's nextStep, expectedOutput, and referenced prompt IDs; the UI must not maintain a competing hard-coded prompt routing table.
Users may mark the current prompt step complete for the browser session; completion is sessionStorage-only, does not mutate the repository, and remains accessible and reduced-motion safe.
The tutorial entry point has an obvious steady glow on ordinary displays and a non-animated but still visible state when reduced motion is requested.
Favorite, Open, and Copy are rendered inside one explicit action rail with reserved desktop header space and a static touch layout on narrow screens so controls cannot overlap.
A successful clipboard write produces a green glowing confirmation toast and a bounded green card-flash animation, with reduced-motion support.

Legacy requirement ID retained for compatibility: Prompt identities and seq values remain stable; discoveryRank remains recommendation metadata only, while the canonical library defaults to ascending numeric sequence.

P65 provides the bounded conversational recommendation workflow and P64 registers the repository tutorial-portfolio ranking prompt; browser route coverage remains live-registry-driven rather than duplicating P65's prompt vocabulary.
Repository guidance exposes the public browser app, phone launcher, direct main ZIP download, direct Windows CMD download, and a one-command main clone path.
The checked-in Prompt Kit website contains the exact canonical base, adaptive guided-questionnaire, journey-guidance, and polish behavior sources after regeneration.

proof_ceiling: Deterministic registry, shared-search recommendation, adaptive route selection, all-prompt specialist reachability, chronological display, explicit Favorites filtering, registry-owned next-step routing, session-only completion state, layout markers, Node syntax, generated-site parity, acquisition documentation, and CI proof. Physical browser rendering, clipboard permissions, assistive-technology coverage, device installation, recommendation quality for every human phrasing, and user acceptance remain field gates.
